seoTitle: How to Make Facebook Reels in Canva (2026)
metaDescription: Make a Facebook Reel in Canva from a template, then post it straight to Facebook or download it as MP4. Covers Pro-only templates, the 250 MB share limit, and Facebook's 2025 change that made every video a reel.
intro:
Canva's Reels templates arrive with the vertical frame, motion and pacing already built, so most of the work is swapping in your own photos, clips and words. This guide follows that route from Canva's home screen to a finished video, then covers the two ways to get it onto Facebook: sharing straight from the editor, or downloading an MP4 and uploading it yourself.

One change to know before you start. In June 2025 Facebook renamed its Videos tab to Reels, and every video posted to Facebook is now shared as a reel, at any length or orientation. Vertical 9:16 is still the shape that fills a phone screen, which is why the templates use it.
costNote: You can build, download and share a Reel on Canva Free. Templates and elements marked with a crown are Pro content: on a free account they carry a watermark until you buy that element or upgrade. Free accounts also download MP4 at the default 1080p only (changing quality triggers an upgrade prompt), which matches Meta's recommended resolution anyway. Scheduling posts through Canva's Content Planner needs Canva Pro, Teams or Nonprofits.

steps.heading: Search for a Facebook Reels template
steps.body: From Canva's home screen (the "What will you learn today?" page), you could open the Video shortcut, but typing "Facebook Reels" into the search bar is quicker. The results split into your own matching Designs and a large grid of Canva Templates.

image.caption: Canva's home dashboard, with format shortcuts across the top and recent designs listed below.

steps.heading: Pick a template for its pacing, and watch for the crown
steps.body:
Each template thumbnail plays a preview on hover. Judge it on pacing and transition style, not just the still frame: colours and text are easy to change later, but rebuilding animation timing from scratch is slow.

Look at the small icon in the bottom corner of each thumbnail. A crown means Pro content. On a free account you can still edit it, but those elements will be watermarked when you download unless you pay for them or upgrade.

image.caption: Search results for "Facebook Reels," showing a grid of vertical video templates with play previews and small crown icons marking Pro templates.

steps.heading: Replace the media and rewrite the text
steps.body:
Drag your own photos or clips from Uploads onto the template's image frames. The new media takes that slot's crop and motion, so it inherits the template's timing.

Then click a text layer and open the Font panel. Document fonts sit at the top, followed by recommended and recently used fonts, and the Text styles tab keeps headings and captions consistent. Rewrite the placeholder copy (here, "Check out our latest reel showcasing the newest additions to our store!") so it names the actual product or announcement.

image.caption: The Font panel open inside a Reel template, with the Animate option in the top toolbar and the 0:10 play bar under the canvas.

steps.heading: Tighten the timing and add audio
steps.body:
Select an element and click Animate in the top toolbar to change how it enters and exits. The play bar under the canvas shows the total length (0:10 in this template). Play it through once and trim anything that lingers.

Add a track from Canva's audio library or upload a voiceover, then trim it to the length of the video and set the volume. If you use paid audio, Canva advises verifying the licence when you download so the post doesn't draw a copyright claim.

steps.heading: Share it to Facebook, or download the MP4
steps.body:
To post from Canva, click Share, then See all, and choose Facebook. The first time, click Connect, log in and allow access. You may be able to add a caption and pick which page of the design to post. Canva's Facebook sharing accepts MP4 video up to 250 MB.

To post it yourself instead, click Share, then Download, choose MP4 Video and keep Quality at 1080p. Meta recommends .mp4 at 1080p for reels, so the default is already right. Watch the file on your phone before posting. That's the screen most people will see it on.

troubleshooting.problem: Facebook isn't listed in the Share menu
troubleshooting.cause: On Canva for Education accounts, social media publishing is off by default and must be enabled by an admin.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask the admin to enable the Facebook app, or download the MP4 and upload it to Facebook directly.

troubleshooting.problem: The downloaded video has a watermark
troubleshooting.cause: The template or some of its elements are Pro content (marked with a crown), and you're on Canva Free.
troubleshooting.fix: Swap those elements for free ones, buy them individually with Remove watermarks, or upgrade. Pro users who still see watermarks may be signed in to the wrong team.

troubleshooting.problem: Sharing to Facebook fails on a longer video
troubleshooting.cause: Canva's direct share to Facebook caps video files at 250 MB.
troubleshooting.fix: Shorten the video, or download the MP4 and upload it through Facebook yourself.

faq.question: How long can a Facebook Reel be?
faq.answer: Since June 2025, every video posted to Facebook is shared as a reel, and Meta says reels can be any length or orientation. Short and tightly paced still suits the format; many Canva templates default to about 10 seconds.

faq.question: Can I post a Reel to Facebook directly from Canva?
faq.answer: Yes. Click Share, See all, then Facebook, and connect your account the first time. The video must be MP4 and 250 MB or smaller.

faq.question: What size and format should I export?
faq.answer: MP4 at 1080p in a vertical 9:16 design. Meta recommends .mp4, 1080p and 24 to 60 frames per second for reels.

faq.question: Is making a Facebook Reel in Canva free?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as you avoid crown-marked Pro content or pay for it per element. Scheduling posts in Content Planner is a paid feature.

verifiedNote: Screens and click path come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2026. Sharing, download and watermark behaviour were re-checked against Canva's help center, and reel specifications against Meta's Business Help Centre, in September 2026. That check added Facebook's June 2025 change (all videos are now reels, any length or orientation), Canva's 250 MB limit for sharing video to Facebook, and the Pro-template watermark rule, and replaced the earlier export-only ending with Canva's direct Share to Facebook option.
